# 2 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_015_page_001.jpg

---

**15:1** When Nicanor found out that Judas and his men were in the region of Samaria, he decided to attack them on the day of rest, when he could do it in complete safety.

**15:2** The Jews who had been forced to march with him protested: "Don't destroy people in this savage and barbarous way. Show respect for the day the All-seeing has made holy and set above all other days."

**15:3** The three-times-cursed wretch shot back: "Is there some sovereign up in heaven who gave an order about the Sabbath?"

**15:4** They answered, "Yes — the living Lord himself, the sovereign of heaven. He commanded the seventh day to be kept."

**15:5** "And I am sovereign on earth," he replied, "and I order you to take up arms and carry out the king's business." But his plan came to nothing.

**15:6** Nicanor, bursting with arrogance and pride, had already decided to set up a public trophy celebrating his victory over Judas and his men.

**15:7** Maccabeus, for his part, never stopped trusting with absolute certainty that the Lord would help him.

**15:8** He kept urging his men not to be afraid of the Gentile attack. He reminded them of all the times heaven had come to their aid before. He told them to expect victory and help from the Almighty.

**15:9** Drawing encouragement from the law and the prophets, calling to mind the battles they had already won, he fired them with enthusiasm.

**15:10** Once he had them stirred up, he gave his instructions — pointing out at the same time how the Gentiles had acted in bad faith and broken their oaths.

**15:11** He equipped each man, not so much with shields and spears, as with bold words of encouragement. He lifted their spirits by sharing a vision — a dream worth believing — that went like this:

**15:12** He saw Onias, the former high priest — a good and noble man, modest in bearing, gentle in manner, gracious in speech, trained from boyhood in everything that shapes excellence — standing with his hands spread out, praying for all the Jewish people.

**15:13** Then, in the same way, there appeared another man — white-haired, dignified, radiating a kind of extraordinary majesty.

**15:14** Onias said: "This is the one who loves the brotherhood and prays constantly for the people and the holy city — Jeremiah, the prophet of God."

**15:15** Jeremiah reached out his right hand and gave Judas a golden sword. As he gave it he said:

**15:16** "Take this holy sword — God's gift — with which you will shatter your enemies."

**15:17** Judas's words were powerful — they could set souls on fire and make young men brave. Stirred by what they had heard, the men decided not to hold back but to charge in boldly and settle things through a fight to the finish — because the city, the sanctuary, and the holy vessels were all on the line.

**15:18** Their concern for wives and children, brothers and relatives — that was real. But what gripped them most, what came first in their hearts, was the holy sanctuary.

**15:19** In the city, too, people were not free from anguish. They were anxious about the battle that was about to happen in the open field.

**15:20** Now everyone was waiting for the final reckoning. The enemy had drawn close. The army was formed up. The war elephants were positioned where they would do the most damage. The cavalry was out on the wings.

**15:21** Maccabeus looked at the forces in front of him — the weapons, the ferocity of the war animals — and stretched his hands up toward heaven. He called on the Lord who works wonders, knowing that victory doesn't come from weapons, but is God's to give to whoever he chooses.

**15:22** He prayed aloud: "You, O Lord, sent your angel in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he struck down 185,000 in the camp of Sennacherib.

**15:23** So now, O Sovereign of heaven, send a good angel before us — to bring fear and trembling.

**15:24** Strike down with your mighty arm those who come with such blasphemy against your holy people." With that he stopped.

**15:25** Nicanor and his army advanced with trumpets blaring and battle songs.

**15:26** Judas and his men went forward to meet them with prayer and invocation.

**15:27** Hands fighting, hearts praying — they cut down no fewer than thirty-five thousand and returned in tremendous joy at what God had done.

**15:28** When the battle was over and they were coming back with celebration, they found Nicanor lying dead in his armor.

**15:29** Shouting broke out. There was noise and rejoicing everywhere. They praised the Sovereign Lord in their ancestral language.

**15:30** Judas — the man who had been his people's chief champion from his youth up, who had never stopped loving his compatriots — gave the order for Nicanor's head and his arm, severed at the shoulder, to be brought to Jerusalem and put on display.

**15:31** When he arrived there, he called together his fellow citizens and placed the priests in front of the altar. Then he summoned those who were in the citadel

**15:32** and showed them Nicanor's head — the head of the vile man — and the arm of the blasphemer who had stretched it up in arrogance against the holy house of the Almighty.

**15:33** He cut out the tongue of the godless Nicanor and said he would give it to the birds in pieces. He hung the proof of his idiocy up opposite the sanctuary.

**15:34** Everyone looked up to heaven and praised the glorious Lord, saying, "Blessed is the one who has kept his own place undefiled."

**15:35** Nicanor's head was hung on the citadel — an unmistakable, visible sign for everyone of the Lord's help.

**15:36** They voted unanimously never to let this day pass without marking it — the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, called Adar in Aramaic, the day before Mordecai's day.

**15:37** That is how things went with Nicanor. From that time on, the city has been in the possession of the Hebrews. And here I bring my story to a close.

**15:38** If the work is well composed and to the point, that is exactly what I was aiming for. If it is inadequate and falls short, it was simply the best I could do.

**15:39** You know how it is with wine: drinking it straight is harmful, and so is drinking water straight. But mix wine with water and the result is both pleasant and enjoyable. In the same way, the style of a story makes it a delight to the ears. And with that — this is where we end.
